source.title: Jitter: Random Jittering Loss Function
source.authors: Zhicheng Cai; Cheng-Lei Peng; Si-Dan Du

record.tranche_reason: The study reports test-loss trajectories over training epochs, using a different measure from the claim's test-error measure.
record.gate_note: The epoch-trajectory findings are test loss, not test error, so they are recorded under fits_no_version rather than linked to V2. The accuracy table compares training methods but does not report a double-descent trajectory. The paper also discusses model-size and data-related double descent, but those statements are background or citations, not its own tests.
record.test_reason: This is a regularization-method paper (Jitter, a random variant of flooding). Its only double-descent result is a test-loss curve over epochs on CIFAR-10 (Fig. 4), and its own loss function produces that curve. It reports no epoch-wise test-error trajectory and no sweep over model size or sample size. The finding concerns a related construct: test loss under a method built to stop training loss reaching zero. So it goes under fits_no_version, not V2. The baseline curve (r1) also gives only test loss, so it cannot show whether test error follows V2.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that Jitter improves test accuracy over the plain method and over flooding on six datasets. They also say it can make the test loss descend a second time and converge, so training stays useful after training error reaches zero. They note that Jitter S shows no double descent and has the lowest test loss but the highest test error.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains VGG16 with a stochastic Jitter loss and reports test-loss trajectories; it does not reproduce a model-size, training-error/interpolation-threshold, or sample-size sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: The CIFAR-10 test-loss trajectory differs across Jitter 1, Jitter 5, and Jitter S.

fits_no_version.finding: On CIFAR-10 with VGG16, the test loss over epochs: rises from about epoch 40 with the plain loss; shows a clear second descent with Jitter 1; stays flat after its first rise with Jitter 5; and keeps descending with no double descent under Jitter S.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Flooding-type loss functions that keep training loss above zero can induce a second descent in test loss over epochs, depending on the jitter distribution.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Joint Conference on Neural Network
record.problems: The reported epoch-wise shape findings concern test loss rather than test error. The plotted trajectory comparison is limited to CIFAR-10 and the paper says the variances across five runs were close to zero but does not list them.

untested.parts: No model-size sweep; only VGG16 is trained.
No test-error trajectory over epochs; only test-loss curves under Jitter/flooding-style losses.
No capacity sweep across model classes.
No variation of label noise and no tuning of regularization strength against peaks. Jitter distributions alter the test-loss shape, but that is not the version's claim.

record.verdict_notes: Fig. 1 is a generic illustration of the double-descent curve, not a result of this study. Its double-descent background cites Nakkiran et al. (an original source) and Belkin et al. (an original source), without testing them. The reader's relation 'tests'/T2 is overturned: there are no test-error epoch trajectories, and the shape is induced by the method itself.

versions.untested_parts: Model-size sweep and test error near the interpolation threshold.
The reported epoch trajectories are test loss rather than test error; only CIFAR-10 trajectories for the plotted methods are described.
No training-sample-size sweep near the interpolation threshold.
No capacity sweep across model classes.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested against peak locations.
The paper varies Jitter distributions, but does not test whether label noise or variance drives double descent, whether peaks split, or whether optimally tuned regularization removes them.

rows.subject: VGG16

rows.operation_detail: Train using the original method without Jitter or flooding.
rows.value: The test-loss curve begins ascending at about the 40-th epoch.
rows.note: The paper describes test loss, not test error; this result cannot establish the version's stated measure.
rows.check: Test loss only; the curve is described just as rising from about epoch 40, with no second descent mentioned. Linkage and state are correct; the 'comparator' role is fine.

rows.value: The test-loss curve exhibits double descent clearly.
rows.note: The described trajectory is test loss, not test error.
rows.check: The shape is produced by the authors' Jitter loss and measured in test loss, not test error. Linkage is correct.

rows.subject: VGG16

rows.operation_detail: Train with Jitter 5, sampling from a standard normal distribution and applying a correction factor of 1e-1.
rows.value: The test loss remains virtually unchanged after its first ascent.
rows.note: The described trajectory is test loss, not test error.
rows.check: Correct as recorded. It is test loss under the method's own loss function.
